description: Switch frontend hosting to AWS Amplify Hosting (Hosting/CI-CD only, NOT an Amplify Gen2 backend rebuild) and rewire the SPA to reach the CDK-managed API cross-origin. Since Amplify Hosting serves the frontend from a different origin than the API, the same-origin '/api' assumption no longer holds: enable CORS on the HTTP API for the Amplify domain and point the SPA's API_BASE at the API endpoint. Add an amplify.yml build spec and document the console/CLI setup (real Amplify connect + deploy cannot run in-sandbox). Update the README (Japanese) for the new architecture, admin URL, Cognito bootstrapping, and Amplify Hosting steps. Depends on FEAT-002/003.
steps: Add an amplify.yml at the repo root: a build spec whose frontend build phase generates frontend/config.js from Amplify environment variables at build time, and whose artifacts baseDirectory is `frontend` with files ['**/*']. Concretely, in the build commands write config.js containing window.API_BASE, window.COGNITO_DOMAIN, window.COGNITO_CLIENT_ID from environment variables (e.g. $API_BASE, $COGNITO_DOMAIN, $COGNITO_CLIENT_ID). Since the frontend has no npm build, preBuild can be a no-op (or echo). Keep it minimal. Ensure the generated config.js is what gets deployed (Amplify serves the frontend directory). NOTE: config.js is committed with placeholders for local dev; the Amplify build overwrites it with real values. Document this clearly in comments.

Decide and implement the hosting change in lib/quiz-app-stack.ts. Chosen approach (document the rationale in code comments and README): Amplify Hosting (connected to the Git repo via the console) becomes the frontend host. Remove the S3 static-site + CloudFront distribution + BucketDeployment used purely for frontend hosting, because Amplify now serves the SPA and keeping CloudFront+S3 for the same purpose is redundant idle-ish cost and reintroduces the 403/404->index.html-rewrites-API problem. If removing CloudFront, the API is called cross-origin, so REPLACE the CORS config: set corsPreflight.allowOrigins to a configurable Amplify domain (CfnParameter/prop `amplifyAppUrl`, default '*' is acceptable for this public demo but document tightening to the real Amplify domain) and keep allowMethods GET/POST/OPTIONS and allowHeaders ['content-type','authorization'] (authorization is now needed for the admin route). Remove the now-unused CloudFrontDomain output; add/keep an ApiEndpoint output. Do NOT define an Amplify App L2 in CDK (that needs the @aws-cdk/aws-amplify-alpha module and a Git token); instead the user connects the repo in the Amplify console - documented in README.

Because there is no longer a CloudFront /api/* same-origin path, update frontend/config.js and app.js: API_BASE must point at the API endpoint (the ApiEndpoint CfnOutput value, e.g. https://<id>.execute-api.<region>.amazonaws.com/api). The Amplify build injects this via amplify.yml. Update the config.js comments accordingly. The fetchJson content-type guard in app.js can stay (harmless) but its comment about CloudFront error rewrites should be updated to reflect the new cross-origin setup.

Ensure the Lambda json() responses include CORS headers that work cross-origin: keep 'access-control-allow-origin' (currently '*'); since the admin route needs the Authorization header, confirm the API CORS allowHeaders includes 'authorization' and the response headers do not block it. (API Gateway HTTP API handles OPTIONS preflight from corsPreflight config; the Lambda proxy responses just need the allow-origin header, already present.)

Update test/quiz-app-stack.test.ts to match the hosting change: if CloudFront + S3 static hosting are removed, remove/replace those assertions (no more AWS::CloudFront::Distribution / api/* behavior / S3 public-access-block for the site bucket). Keep/adjust assertions for DynamoDB on-demand, Lambda ARM64, HTTP API, the 4 routes, Cognito, and the JWT authorizer. Add an assertion that the HTTP API CORS configuration allows the 'authorization' header. Do NOT assert on Amplify resources (Amplify is set up in the console, not CDK).

Rewrite README.md (Japanese) to reflect the NEW architecture: (a) update the architecture diagram to show Amplify Hosting serving the SPA and the browser calling API Gateway cross-origin (with CORS), Cognito User Pool + Hosted UI for admin auth, JWT authorizer on the admin write route; (b) document the admin URL (/admin.html on the Amplify domain) and the admin quiz-creation flow; (c) document Cognito bootstrapping: after cdk deploy, create the first admin user via `aws cognito-idp admin-create-user` (and set a permanent password via `aws cognito-idp admin-set-user-password --permanent`), since self-signup is disabled; note updating the app client callback/logout URLs with the real Amplify domain; (d) document Amplify Hosting setup: connect the Git repo in the Amplify console (Hosting only), set environment variables API_BASE / COGNITO_DOMAIN / COGNITO_CLIENT_ID (from the CDK CfnOutputs), and that amplify.yml drives the build; (e) update deploy/verify/teardown sections and keep the cost-minimization rationale (add Cognito free-tier + Amplify build/hosting cost notes; note S3+CloudFront for the frontend was removed in favor of Amplify Hosting); (f) keep the 'built in a network-blocked sandbox, run these commands on a networked machine' notice with the env -u NODE_OPTIONS caveat.

If any package.json change is needed (it should NOT be, since HttpJwtAuthorizer and cognito are in aws-cdk-lib and Amplify is console-managed), make it minimal and justify it. Prefer NO new dependency.
Run `node --check frontend/config.js` and `node --check frontend/app.js` in-sandbox to confirm plain JS parses.
acceptance_criteria: amplify.yml exists at repo root with a frontend build that generates config.js from Amplify environment variables and serves the frontend/ directory (artifacts baseDirectory frontend).

The CDK stack no longer hosts the frontend via S3+CloudFront (removed) and the HTTP API CORS allows cross-origin calls including the 'authorization' header; ApiEndpoint output remains and the removed CloudFrontDomain output is gone.
frontend/config.js/app.js are wired for a cross-origin API_BASE (API endpoint), with updated comments; content-type guard remains valid.

README.md (Japanese) documents the new architecture, the /admin.html admin URL, Cognito first-admin bootstrapping commands, and the Amplify Hosting console setup + environment variables, plus updated deploy/verify/teardown and cost rationale.
Updated CDK assertion tests reflect the removed CloudFront/S3 hosting and the new CORS/authorization-header expectation, and pass on a networked machine.
No unjustified new npm dependency; `node --check` passes on the frontend JS files.
verification: On a networked machine: `env -u NODE_OPTIONS npm run build && env -u NODE_OPTIONS npm test && env -u NODE_OPTIONS npx cdk synth` all succeed with the updated tests.
Confirm the synthesized template has no AWS::CloudFront::Distribution for the site (if removed) and the HTTP API CORS includes 'authorization' in allowed headers.
In-sandbox: `node --check frontend/config.js` and `node --check frontend/app.js` pass; amplify.yml is valid YAML; README renders and covers admin URL + Cognito bootstrap + Amplify setup.

User acceptance on their machine: connect the repo to Amplify Hosting, set env vars, deploy; visit the Amplify URL for the quiz and /admin.html for the admin flow; confirm cross-origin API calls succeed and the admin route rejects unauthenticated requests (401/403).
findings: Added amplify.yml (version 1, Hosting-only; build phase regenerates frontend/config.js from $API_BASE/$COGNITO_DOMAIN/$COGNITO_CLIENT_ID; artifacts.baseDirectory=frontend, files=['**/*']). Removed the S3 SiteBucket + CloudFront Distribution + BucketDeployment and the s3/s3deploy/cloudfront/origins imports from lib/quiz-app-stack.ts; removed the CloudFrontDomain CfnOutput (kept ApiEndpoint/TableName/UserPool* outputs). Updated HTTP API corsPreflight allowHeaders to ['content-type','authorization'] (methods unchanged GET/POST/OPTIONS, allowOrigins stays ['*'] with a documented note to tighten to the Amplify domain). Rewired frontend: config.js API_BASE default now '' with comments describing the cross-origin full-URL (ApiEndpoint+'/api'); app.js fetchJson content-type guard kept but its CloudFront comment rewritten for the cross-origin setup. Updated test/quiz-app-stack.test.ts: removed CloudFront/S3 assertions, added zero-count assertions for AWS::CloudFront::Distribution and AWS::S3::Bucket, added a CORS AllowHeaders 'authorization' assertion, and asserted CloudFrontDomain output is gone. Rewrote README.md (Japanese) for the Amplify Hosting architecture, /admin.html flow, Cognito bootstrap CLI, Amplify env-var setup, updated deploy/verify/teardown and cost section. Default AWS-architecture seed data (19 questions across 2 quizzes) already satisfied by FEAT-001/002. VERIFICATION: network is INTEGRATIONS_ONLY so npm/tsc/jest/cdk-synth cannot run in-sandbox; verified `node --check` passes for frontend/config.js, app.js, admin.js and amplify.yml structure by inspection. User must run `env -u NODE_OPTIONS npm ci && npm run build && npm test && npx cdk synth` on a networked machine. No new npm dependency added.
